Title: Request OTP and verify OTP
Preconditions: User has a valid email address
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/request-otp with the email address as a query parameter. 2. Send a POST request to /api/auth/verify-otp with the OTP verification request body.

Test Data: {"email": "user@example.com", "otp": "123456"}
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON body containing a success message

Title: Verify that OTP value is not exposed in the API response
Preconditions: User has a valid registered email address
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/request-otp with the query parameter 'email' set to a valid registered email address.

Test Data: email=testuser@example.com
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK), a success message 'OTP sent to your email', and the 'data' field in the response body is null or empty (OTP value is not returned).

Title: Verify that OTP is not leaked in logs or error messages during OTP request
Preconditions: User has a valid registered email address
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/request-otp with the query parameter 'email' set to a valid registered email address. 2. Check server logs and error responses for any exposure of the OTP value.

Test Data: email=testuser@example.com
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK), and no OTP value is visible in server logs, error messages, or any part of the response other than the email delivery system.

Title: Verify that OTP verification enforces rate limiting to prevent brute-force attacks
Preconditions: User has a valid registered email address and a valid OTP has been generated
Steps:
1. Send 10 consecutive POST requests to /api/auth/verify-otp with invalid OTP values in rapid succession. 2. On the 11th request, send a valid OTP.

Test Data: {"phoneNumber": "+1234567890", "otp": "0000"} (repeat with different invalid OTPs)
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 429 (Too Many Requests) after exceeding the rate limit threshold, and the valid OTP request is rejected until the rate limit window resets.

Title: Verify that OTP verification rejects replayed OTPs after successful use
Preconditions: User has a valid registered email address and a valid OTP has been generated and used successfully
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/verify-otp with a valid OTP. 2. Repeat the same request with the same OTP.

Test Data: {"phoneNumber": "+1234567890", "otp": "123456"}
Expected Result: The first request succeeds with HTTP status 200 (OK). The second request fails with HTTP status 401 (Unauthorized) or 403 (Forbidden), indicating the OTP has already been used or expired.

Title: Verify that OTP verification rejects expired OTPs
Preconditions: User has a valid registered email address and an expired OTP has been generated
Steps:
1. Wait until the OTP expires (e.g., 5 minutes after generation). 2. Send a POST request to /api/auth/verify-otp with the expired OTP.

Test Data: {"phoneNumber": "+1234567890", "otp": "123456"}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 401 (Unauthorized) or 403 (Forbidden), indicating the OTP has expired.

Title: Verify that error messages during shop profile retrieval do not leak sensitive system details
Preconditions: User is authenticated and has access to shop profiles
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/areas/999999/shops (where 999999 is a non-existent area ID). 2. Inspect the error response for any internal system details.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 404 (Not Found) and a generic error message (e.g., 'Area not found') without revealing internal system details (e.g., stack traces, database errors, or SQL queries).

Title: Verify that shop profile retrieval enforces proper authorization (insecure direct object reference)
Preconditions: Two users are registered: User A (has access to Shop ID 1) and User B (has no access to Shop ID 1)
Steps: 1. Authenticate as User B. 2. Send a GET request to /api/areas/{areaId}/shops/1 (where areaId is valid for Shop ID 1).
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 (Forbidden) or 404 (Not Found), and no shop details are returned.

Title: Verify removal of Hibernate SQL formatting and debug logging does not break application functionality
Section: Hibernate SQL Formatting and Debug Logging
Preconditions: Application deployed with the updated configuration, database connection established
Steps:
1. Deploy the application with the updated application.properties. 2. Perform database operations (e.g., create, read, update, or delete records). 3. Check application logs to confirm SQL statements are no longer formatted or logged at DEBUG level for org.hibernate.SQL.

Test Data: Removed properties: spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.format_sql=true, logging.level.org.hibernate.SQL=DEBUG
Expected Result: Database operations complete successfully, and logs no longer show formatted SQL or DEBUG-level Hibernate SQL statements.

Title: Verify placeholder references in JWT and mail configurations resolve correctly
Section: JWT and Mail Configuration Placeholder Resolution
Preconditions: Application deployed with the updated configuration, environment variables (if any) set for placeholders
Steps:
1. Deploy the application with the updated application.properties. 2. Trigger operations that use JWT (e.g., user login) and mail (e.g., send a test email). 3. Check application logs for errors related to unresolved placeholders or misconfigured properties.

Test Data: JWT secret: jwt.secret=test-secret, Mail properties: spring.mail.host, spring.mail.port, etc.
Expected Result: JWT authentication and mail operations complete successfully without errors related to unresolved placeholders or misconfigured properties.
